brief: Tonight is Legs B, and it is your fourth training day in a row, so this is a back-off night on the lift that matters most. The RDL comes down: three sets, 135 then 155 twice, instead of last time's four sets up to 180. Your other big hinge already said it was tired — your deadlift went from 265 for 5 twice on 28 August to 255 for 4 twice on 10 September — and your recovery trainer vetoed adding weight tonight. I upheld that veto. 180 for 10 is already banked and 190 is waiting for you after the deload, which starts on 21 September. Everything else is either the same as last time or one normal step up: leg press 130, 150, 170; leg curl keeps its 145 top set and only the opening set moves, 100 to 110; calf press stays at 240, 260, 260 and the job is 15 reps on all three; cable crunch stays at 65 and the job is 12. The hip abductor is the one number I moved down. The app was going to ask you for 142.5 tonight, but that came off two sets from 5 September that were typed into your phone 0.8 seconds apart — remembered after the fact, not recorded as you lifted. Your last real reading there is 110 for 12 on 13 September, so tonight is 110 and we get one honest number to build on. Same reason the hanging leg raise just repeats two sets: stop each one when your form goes, not at a count. One thing to do outside the gym — step on a scale this week. The last bodyweight in the app is 207 lb from 23 August, 24 days ago, and with the show on 1 March that is the one number nobody can guess for you.

flags.note: Fourth training day in a row. Your recovery trainer vetoed adding weight to the RDL on tiredness grounds and I upheld it — three sets tonight topping out at 155, instead of four up to 180.

The hip abductor is set to 110 tonight, not the 142.5 the app would have asked for on its own: the heavier numbers from 5 September were typed in 0.8 seconds apart, so they were recalled, not measured, and your last real reading there is 110 for 12 on 13 September.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August — 207 lb, 24 days ago. Your recovery trainer says it cannot tell whether you are recovering or just grinding without it.

Open question I cannot put on a Yes/No card, because it is about weights rather than program structure: five lifts run on both leg days — leg curl, both hip machines, calf press and cable crunch — and each day is quietly progressing off its own history, so the same muscle carries two different working weights. Nobody has decided whether Legs A is meant to be the lighter day, and until someone does these five will keep drifting apart. That one needs you and me in a session.

Tonight's first slot is still called Smith RDL and this gym has no Smith machine; on 5 September you logged that slot as 'Barbell'. Your program trainer has put a card on it explaining why the name is staying.
Your morning review did not run on 13 September, so that Legs A session went out on the app's standing rules with no trainer on it. Today's review did run.
Meso 2, week 4 of 4 — the last hard week. The deload starts 21 September. Three trainers reported, seven disagreements settled, one tiredness veto upheld, and no pain or injury objection was raised.

proposals.why: The hanging leg raise is the only thing left that makes Legs B different from Legs A, but it sits dead last on a long night, and on 5 September both its sets were typed in a second apart the following afternoon rather than during the session — this moves it ahead of the cable crunch instead of leaving it at the tail.

Both push days now press dumbbells overhead at 8 to 10 reps, and Push B does it first and heaviest, so this takes the Push A sets to 10 to 12 and lets the two days stop being the same session — the same way your chest press already splits 10 to 12 on Push A and 8 to 10 on Push B.

dissent.progression: Both heavy sets hit 180 for 10, the top of the range, so the step to 190 is earned.
dissent.recovery: Cut to three sets and stop at 155 — fourth straight training day, and the deadlift already lost reps last week.
dissent.why: The 190 is genuinely earned on measured sets, so this is not about whether he is strong enough. It is that the only other heavy hinge in the program measurably went backwards between 28 August and 10 September, this is day four with no rest, and there is no bodyweight reading in 24 days to tell recovery from grinding. Three facts pointing the same way beat one earned step, and the cost of waiting is five days — the deload starts on 21 September and 190 is there for him in Meso 3.

dissent.progression: 5 September proved 127.5 and 135 for 15, so the second set goes to 145.
dissent.recovery: Those two sets were entered a second apart from memory — the trustworthy reading is 110 for 12 on 13 September.
dissent.why: I checked the timestamps myself rather than taking either seat's word: the two 5 September sets are 0.83 seconds apart, which is a person typing, not a person lifting. Progression's step was built on invented precision and would have put 145 lb on a machine where his last measured work is 110. Recovery wins outright, and tonight's log gives us the real number.

dissent.progression: Stuck at 12 and 12, the bottom of the range, so add a rep to each set.
dissent.recovery: Last time's two sets of 12 were typed in a second from memory, so nobody knows what he actually did — repeat and stop on form.
dissent.why: Same defect as the abductor, and the progression seat said so itself once I showed it the timestamps: the two sets are 0.98 seconds apart and stamped 6 September at 17:23, about twenty hours after that session's last real set. You cannot add a rep to a rep count nobody recorded.

dissent.progression: All three sets finished at 12, the top of the range, so each goes up one 10 lb step.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 120, 140 and 160 — quads were pressed three days ago and this is day four.
dissent.why: This one is measured, with real minutes between every set, and all three finished at the top of the range. It is a machine press with nowhere to get hurt, the step is the standard 10 lb, and I have already taken the load off the hinge that starts the night — so the session as a whole is lighter than last time even with this raise in it.

dissent.progression: Hold the 145 top set until it gives 12, and move the opening set from 100 to 110.
dissent.recovery: Two sets at 130 — hamstrings twice in four days and the RDL comes first tonight.
dissent.why: Recovery's argument was that the RDL would already have taxed the hamstrings, and I have just cut the RDL to 155 for three sets, which removes most of that. Nothing here adds weight to the top set; the only change is the warm-up set, and 130 for 12 twice on 13 September proves 110 is not a hard opener.

dissent.progression: Same weights as last time — 260 is not finished until all three sets give 15.
dissent.recovery: Stay at 240 rather than chasing 260 on a fourth straight day.
dissent.why: Nothing goes up here either way, so the question is only whether to go backwards. He already did 260 for 15 on a measured set on 5 September; dropping to 240 would take away work he has proven. Calves are also the least fatiguing thing on tonight's card.

dissent.progression: Same 65 for three sets, and 12 reps is what earns more weight.
dissent.recovery: Same 65, but two sets is enough with abs already worked this week.
dissent.why: The weight is not in dispute — only the third set is. Abs are the cheapest sets in the session and the slot asks for three. If the fourth straight day shows up anywhere, it will not be in a cable crunch.

overrides.reason: Fourth training day in a row and your deadlift lost reps last week, so this is a deliberate back-off: three sets, topping at 155 instead of 180. Your 180 for 10 is banked and 190 is the target after the deload.
All three sets finished at 12 last time, the top of the range, so each one goes up one 10 lb step. Start at 10 reps and work back up to 12.

145 only gave 10 reps last time, so the top set stays where it is until it gives 12. The one change is the opening set: you did 130 for 12 twice on 13 September, so 100 is too light and it moves to 110.

The heavier 5 September numbers were typed into your phone 0.8 seconds apart, so they were recalled rather than measured and I will not build on them. Your last real reading is 110 for 12 on 13 September — tonight is 110 for two sets, and what you log becomes the number we use.
Both trainers agree here: 105 on 5 September for 12 and 105 again on 13 September for 13. The weight stays and the job tonight is 15 on both sets.
Nothing goes up. You got 260 for 15 once on 5 September and then dropped to 13 on the last set, so 260 is not finished — same three weights, and the job is 15 on all three.
65 for 10 on 5 September and 65 for 11 on 13 September — the reps are climbing but 12 is the number that earns more weight. Hold 65 and get 12 on all three sets.
Last time's two sets of 12 were typed in a second apart from memory, so there is no real reading to add a rep to. Repeat two bodyweight sets and stop each one when your form goes, not at a count.
